strategies.name: Baseline Sequential All-Reduce Chain
strategies.desc: Performs 8 sequential all-reduce operations with interleaved local bidiagonal coupling and inverse operations. Each stage does one all-reduce dispatch followed by local element-wise operations. Total 8 all-reduce dispatches. Represents the reference pattern with no fusion or overlap—simplest correctness path but highest latency.

strategies.name: Fused Local Computation Between Collectives
strategies.desc: Merges the inverse bidiagonal operation of stage i with the forward bidiagonal operation of stage i+1 into a single local kernel before each all-reduce (except first and last). Reduces local compute dispatches from 16 to 9 while keeping 8 all-reduce dispatches. Trades kernel fusion complexity for reduced host-device synchronization overhead.

strategies.name: Chunked Reduce-Scatter All-Gather Pipeline
strategies.desc: Replaces each all-reduce with a reduce-scatter followed by all-gather pair, enabling rank-local shard ownership during the bidiagonal coupling phase. Each rank computes its owned shard's coupling locally, reducing cross-rank data movement. Total 16 collective dispatches (8 RS + 8 AG) but each operates on 1/W payload size, optimizing bandwidth utilization at scale.

strategies.name: Hierarchical Two-Level Reduction Tree
strategies.desc: Exploits potential node structure by performing intra-node all-reduce (within num_devices cores) followed by inter-node all-reduce across num_nodes groups, then broadcast back. Applies bidiagonal coupling at node granularity where possible. Expected ~16 dispatches (8 stages × 2 levels) but with smaller effective world sizes per collective, reducing latency via topology awareness.

strategies.name: Batched All-Reduce with Deferred Coupling
strategies.desc:
Batches multiple stage results into a single larger tensor and issues fewer all-reduce calls on concatenated buffers, deferring the coupling/inverse transformations until after batch reduction completes. Reduces all-reduce count from 8 to 2-4 by concatenating stage inputs, trading increased memory footprint (O(stages) buffers) for lower collective overhead and better NIC utilization through larger messages.
